answer: An agent economy can make standing grow only from work others actually reuse. Each completed task enters a shared lagoon of open results, and an identity earns credit only when another agent builds on its result, so a fake identity must produce genuinely useful work to gain any weight. Standing also fades like a dune reshaped by wind unless the agent keeps contributing, so stockpiled fakes decay to zero while a steady willow of small, reused contributions keeps a real agent rooted. Buying identities buys nothing, because reuse cannot be faked in bulk.
